name: Contact Physics
author: Kizi
description: What happens to a car in contact. Two models: Rigid body (mass, inertia, bounce, friction, rubbing tyres) or Classic (the 0.5 spin and tyre lift). Walls, aero loss, damage. AI driving: AI Driver Behaviour.

options.label: Physics: contact model
options.description: Rigid body = every touch calculated from both cars' mass, speed and contact point. Classic = the 0.5 contact: set spin, twitch and tyre lift effects (cars fly more on tyre contact).

options.label: Rigid body: strength
options.description: How strong car contact is. Normal = tuned values (tyre friction 1.8, bodies 0.6, bounce 0.25). x1.5 / x2 / x3 scale bounce and friction (bounce max 0.8, friction max 3.0). Rigid body only.

options.label: Rigid body: bounce
options.description: How much cars bounce apart after a hit: 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.4 of the closing speed. Rigid body only.

options.label: Rigid body: friction
options.description: Grip between the touching parts: tyre on tyre 1.8, bodies 0.6 at Medium (Low x0.5, High x1.5). Rigid body only.

options.label: Rigid body: tyre rotation
options.description: Rolling tyre surfaces rub in tyre-on-tyre touches (rubber on rubber), like real wheel-over-wheel contact: a chasing car can climb the tyre ahead and launch. Rigid body only.

options.label: Rigid body: push AI cars
options.description: On = AI cars take the push too and AI-AI touches count. Off = only your car is pushed (the game's own rule). Rigid body only.

options.label: Rigid body: game's own response
options.description: Add = the game's own solver pushes the cars apart, so hits cause damage, and we add bounce, friction and the tyre rub (recommended). Ignore = ours only, no damage from car hits. Rigid body only.

options.label: Classic: AI spin from hits
options.description: Adds the yaw a hit would give an AI car, from where the cars touched and how fast they closed. Light, Medium or Strong. Classic only.

options.label: Classic: twitch when hit
options.description: Gives every AI car in a contact at least a small yaw twitch. Needs "AI spin from hits" on. Classic only.

options.label: Classic: who spins
options.description: Which car of a touching pair gets the extra spin: both, only the car behind (the one that hit), or only the car ahead (the one that was hit). Classic only.

options.label: Classic: rear hit spins the car ahead
options.description: When the car ahead is hit behind its centre (a hit on the rear tyre), it gets at least this much spin, so a punt from behind can send it round. Classic only.

options.label: Classic: wheel-over-wheel lift
options.description: When a tyre rides up on another car, the car behind is lifted at the wheel that touched (a rear-wheel touch lifts the rear). This is the old flying on tyre contact. Classic only.

options.label: Classic: wheel-to-wheel push
options.description: Touching tyres push the cars apart (the game ships this off, and only pushes your car). Subtle to Extreme; Extreme can throw cars. Classic only.

options.label: Contact: applies to
options.description: Which touches get the contact physics, punctures and the AI's reaction: all of them (AI against AI too), or only touches with you. Both models.

options.label: Contact: softening
options.description: The game softens every car-to-car hit with two assists. Off = hits are not softened.

options.label: Walls: wall physics
options.description: Cars scrape along walls (friction) and barriers absorb most of a hit's energy, so a car does not bounce back off a wall like a pinball.

options.label: Aero: loss when sideways
options.description: Wings only work with air from the front. A car sliding sideways or backwards loses most of its downforce, so spins slide further. Realistic: down to 30 %. Strong: 12 %.

options.label: Damage: energy-based wing damage
options.description: Hard car-to-car hits add front-wing damage that grows with the energy of the hit (speed squared), on top of the game's own. Rigid body only.

options.label: Damage: equal damage for AI cars
options.description: The game gives AI cars a different damage factor than your car. On = every AI car takes the same damage from a hit as your car would (wing, body parts, suspension).

options.label: Damage: tyre punctures
options.description: A hit at a tyre can give it a puncture, the more likely the harder the touch (touches under 10 km/h never do, full chance from 60 km/h). Uses the game's own puncture, so the tyre loses air and may burst.

options.label: Damage: punctures can hit you
options.description: Off = only AI cars get punctures from contact. On = your tyres too.

options.label: Damage: suspension after a jump
options.description: A car that flies (over a wheel, a kerb, another car) can land with damaged suspension. Longer flights and harder landings are more likely. Off / Rare / Sometimes / Often.

options.label: Damage: jump damage level
options.description: Damage = one corner badly damaged, the car keeps going but handles worse. Break = the corner reaches the game's own breaking point (a wheel can come off).

options.label: Damage: jumps can damage your car
options.description: Off = only AI cars get suspension damage from jumps. On = your car too.

options.label: Damage: leave suspension to Terminal Damage
options.description: When the Terminal Damage addon is installed, this addon changes no suspension damage (no jump damage, no AI suspension factors), so Terminal Damage's own suspension model stays in charge.

options.label: Testing: log contacts
options.description: Writes every car-to-car touch to swofty\loader.log (who touched, how hard, how far each car turned). Only for testing; leave off.
